subject: Linear A undeciphered writing system

core_connection.name: STRUCTURAL_INVARIANCE_UNDER_CORPUS_PARTITION
core_connection.observation: Modern Linear A analysis can extract linguistic/structural information without a full decipherment by comparing repeated structural patterns, syntax/orthography, and syllabotactic behavior across independently partitioned regional corpora.
core_connection.external_basis: A 2026 Cambridge analysis divides the Linear A corpus into five regional corpora centered on major Minoan palaces and compares them with one another; an analogous Linear B analysis is used as a control.
core_connection.epistemic_boundary: Structural regularity and cross-corpus consistency are not a full decipherment.

secondary_connections.name: FORMULA_VARIANTS_REVEAL_ROLE_WITHOUT_FULL_DECIPHERMENT
secondary_connections.observation: Repeated Linear A offering formulas with subtle vessel-to-vessel variation can be compared to infer likely grammatical roles while lexical meaning remains unresolved.
secondary_connections.boundary: Role inference is not semantic translation.

secondary_connections.name: RELATED_SIGN_MEMORY_REQUIRES_CONTEXTUAL_VALIDATION
secondary_connections.observation: Some Linear A signs overlap with Linear B, but the undeciphered status requires contextual validation before any provisional reading is promoted.
secondary_connections.boundary: Sign similarity is a hypothesis generator, not sufficient evidence for linguistic identity.

secondary_connections.name: STRUCTURE_CAN_BE_INFORMATIVE_WHILE_SEMANTICS_REMAINS_OPEN
secondary_connections.observation: Linear A has documented sign inventory, directionality, numerical conventions, syntax hypotheses, orthography, regional regularities and recurring formulaic structure despite remaining undeciphered.
secondary_connections.boundary: The method does not imply that every unresolved system is decipherable from structure alone.

meta_registry_matches.reason: Linear A provides an external example where structural signal can survive corpus partition; JANUS already treats representation as a mediator of detectability.
Both use related prior material and multiple comparisons to constrain interpretation without treating a provisional score/reading as universal truth. Operator-level analogy only.
Linear A cleanly separates structural evidence from unresolved semantics.
Regional partitioning behaves like a structural split control: effects that survive held-out partitions are less dependent on one local subset.

new_janus_operator.name: PARTITION_SURVIVAL_GATE
new_janus_operator.definition: A candidate connection gains confidence when it survives multiple domain- or corpus-preserving partitions while an appropriate control corpus does not inherit the same structure merely from shared formatting.

why_nontrivial: The external corpus was not authored as a JANUS registry artifact and was not constructed to instantiate JANUS terminology. This therefore tests whether the operator generalizes outside the registry's own vocabulary and data-generation process.
negative_controls: Do not use Unicode character names as semantic meanings.
Do not treat Linear B equivalents as a full Linear A translation.
Do not infer authorial intent from visual similarity between scripts.
Do not promote cross-region regularity into a decipherment claim.

recommended_experiment.name: LINEAR_A_PARTITION_BLIND_REPLICA
procedure: Encode Linear A inscriptions by corpus-standard identifiers and sequence structure, not translated glosses.
Split the corpus by region or archaeological context.
Extract the candidate structural operator independently in each partition.
Repeat with Linear B as a positive control and a schema-matched synthetic corpus as null.
Blind the detector to script names and Unicode character names before final scoring.
recommended_experiment.success_condition: The same structural operator persists across held-out Linear A partitions while the matched null substantially weakens or removes it.
recommended_experiment.claim_ceiling: A successful test establishes transportability of the structural operator, not decipherment.
